The First Conditional vs. The Second Conditional

You use the first conditional to talk about real situations in the present or future.

You use the second conditional to talk about unreal or imaginary (hypothetical) situations in the future.

First conditional form:
If + Simple Present verb, + will
If you come over, I'll help you with that.
(you can come over)

Second conditional form:
If + Simple Past verb, + would
If you had time, I would help you with that.
(I don't think or I know you don't have time)

In conversation, it is common to use contractions. (I would = I'd)
The Future with Will, Going to, and the Present Continuous
You can use three different tenses to talk about the future.
When you talk about things that are not decided or when you make a decision at the moment of speaking for the future, you use the modal will.
When you ask about intentions, you use be going to.
When you talk about things that are arranged, on the agenda or booked for the future, you use the Present Continuous tense.
